headline: Asia: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Asia: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
- South Asia: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution.
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy: Russia thanked US for easing sanctions by bombing Zaporizhzhia.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: Soldiers intervene on roadside to save children from alleged knife attack.
Three soldiers sprang into action when a highway crash in Washington turned into a knife attack on two children.
The Caribbean - bottom line: StJMC mulls action against companies for hanging wires.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: StJMC mulls action against companies for hanging wires.
WESTERN BUREAU: The St James Municipal Corporation is calling on telecommunications companies with low-hanging wires, which were displaced by Hurricane Melissa a year ago, to address them immediately or risk legal action in the interest of the public safety. Montego Bay Mayor Richard Vernon issued the warning on Thursday at the St James Municipal Corporation’s (StJMC) City Hall 2026 Municipal Budget Presentation at the Montego Bay Cultural Centre, where he outlined plans for the corporation’s $2.8-billion budget expenditure for the 2027-2028 financial year.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia responded to the easing of US sanctions with deadly strikes on Zaporizhzhia, where 12 people have been killed.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Zelenskyy after speaking with Macron: threat of missile strikes remains particularly high in coming days.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has discussed the challenges posed by the easing of US sanctions on Russian oil products with French President Emmanuel Macron.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russians hit restaurant building in Kyiv during missile attack, leaving 6 injured.
Debris from a drone reportedly fell on a 25-storey residential building and an eight-storey office building in Kyiv's Solomianskyi district, and later a restaurant was hit during a missile strike.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia: twenty killed, including three children – photo.
The death toll following the Russian airstrike on Zaporizhzhia has risen to 20, including three children, and 18 others have been injured.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Germany warns EU that €159B budget cuts are not enough.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Germany warns EU that €159B budget cuts are not enough.
Frugal countries said an end-of-year agreement is less likely after Ireland's proposal.

Western intelligence assessments suggest Iran has preserved key weapons factories and can replenish its missile arsenal despite months of US-Israeli attacks.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation suspends airpot operations following airstrikes.
A loud explosion was reported at Riyadh's main airport as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified, with airlines canceling flights and passengers urged to check their flight status.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Ethiopian-Eritrean fighting raises fears of wider war as Egypt builds Red Sea alliance - analysis.
Drone strikes in northern Ethiopia, competing claims over Red Sea access, and a new four-country diplomatic alignment threaten to deepen instability across the Horn of Africa.
- Jerusalem Post, South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: Three injured in Poland's third youth stabbing attack in four days.
A 21-year-old student allegedly stabbed three people at a Warsaw college, days after two school attacks left one person dead and several injured, raising fears of further violence.
Africa - bottom line: Kenyan health ministry urges churches to raise awareness about Ebola.
- Africanews, 3 hours ago: Kenyan health ministry urges churches to raise awareness about Ebola.
This follows the death in Nairobi on Monday of a Kenyan man who had travelled home from DR Congo through Uganda.

Panama was hit by a powerful 7.7 earthquake, a 6.6 aftershock and many tremors, damaging buildings and prompting evacuations but no deaths reported.
- Africanews, 9 hours ago: Rare waterspouts slam western Sicily, wrecking homes and a school.
A rare pair of waterspouts swept ashore in western Sicily on Friday, damaging homes, vehicles and a school. The two funnels formed off the coast near Marsala before moving inland towards Trapani, hitting the town of Petrosino along the way.

- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, ABC News Australia, Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Guardian - Australia, one hour ago: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said on Saturday, a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine. Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said on Saturday. At least 18 people were wounded in the attack. Missiles also struck Kyiv in a daytime...

Chinese military aircraft may already be using a new joint aviation facility in Laos, with satellite imagery showing twice as many K-8/JL-8-family trainer aircraft there as the Laotian air force is assessed to possess. Eight of the two-seat trainer and light-attack aircraft were visible at Ban Keun Airport in commercial satellite imagery taken on September 30, according to Reuters, which first reported the images. South Asia - bottom line: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: Trump sows doubt on plan to livestream US military execution.
US President Donald Trump has cast doubt on whether authorities will livestream the firing squad execution of the perpetrator of a deadly attack on American soldiers, a plan that has drawn broad and bipartisan condemnation, it emerged on Saturday. Nidal Hasan’s execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: 10 terrorists killed during CTD operation in Barkhan, says Balochistan govt.
QUETTA: Ten terrorists were killed in a targeted intelligence-based operation conducted by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in Balochistan’s Barkhan district, the Home Department said on Saturday. An aide in the Home Department, Babar Yousafzai, said: “During an intense gun battle, 10 armed terrorists were killed and two CTD officials were injured.” The CTD had conducted a targeted operation after receiving credible information about the presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al Hindustan, in the area, according to Yousafzai.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Pakistan reaffirms commitment to Saudi security at UN Security Council.
UNITED NATIONS: Pakistan has reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), declaring that it would stand “shoulder to shoulder” with the kingdom in the face of continued Houthi attacks.

The attacks on October 8 were the deadliest in Saudi Arabia since the kingdom and allied forces in neighbouring Yemen launched a major military offensive against Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels last weekend

The Minnesota Vikings are 4-0, but Rob Parker believes their poor offense makes them the NFL’s weakest unbeaten team. Two victories without an offensive touchdown have raised concerns, even as their defense and kicker Will Reichard keep delivering results. Minnesota now needs to improve its attack to prove its perfect start reflects genuine strength.
